stem: A 5-year-old girl is brought in because her teacher has noticed episodes of staring and ‘day-dreaming’ during class and choir practice. Her mother has also seen brief staring spells that occur mid-sentence; the child pauses for a few seconds and then immediately resumes what she was doing. There is no fall, postictal drowsiness, colour change, or developmental regression. In the office, she has a 5-second staring spell after hyperventilation and then fully recovers. Which anti-seizure medication would you recommend?
explanation: This is classic childhood absence epilepsy: brief staring spells, provoked by hyperventilation, with immediate recovery and no postictal phase. Ethosuximide is first-line for typical absence seizures in a child with absence-only seizures.
rationale: The vignette describes typical absence seizures (brief staring spells, hyperventilation trigger, no postictal state). Ethosuximide is the preferred first-line agent when absence seizures are the only seizure type.

optionExplanations.A: Carbamazepine is used for focal seizures and can worsen absence seizures.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: first-line treatment for typical absence seizures.
optionExplanations.C: Levetiracetam (Keppra) is not first-line for classic absence epilepsy.
optionExplanations.D: Sodium valproate can treat absence seizures but is generally reserved when broader seizure coverage is needed or ethosuximide is unsuitable.

Instructions

Question 4 - 6 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 5-year old girl is brought in by her mother to see you because her teacher has been concerned that she has been having ‘day-dreams’ in choir practise and also during class. Her mother has also noted ‘day dreams’ which have been occurring mid-sentence associated with staring off in the distance. The ‘day dreams’ last a few seconds and then she is back to normal and continues on with her sentence. She doesn’t fall and doesn’t get sleepy after the events. She has no colour change. The girl is otherwise developmentally normal and got a good mid-year report from school. On examination her height and weight are on the 75

th

centile. She has a completely normal examination. You get the patient to blow up a balloon in your office and she has a staring spell that lasts 5seconds before she completely recovers.
